proposition: The HELOC was originated in July 2022 by Lendage, LLC in the amount of $149,650.00
supporting_pinpoints: Doc. 34 at 3 n.4; ledger p.5 row 08/05/22
what_the_document_actually_shows: Doc. 34 states it as background; the ledger books an opening principal balance of $149,650.00 on 08/05/22
what_is_claimed_from_it: That a $149,650.00 loan was made and funded
gap_between_the_two: The ledger shows a BALANCE was established. It does not show that $149,650.00 in proceeds was delivered to anyone. Those are different facts, and the difference is exactly what Judge Bagley said the claims turn on.
admissibility_concerns: The ledger is a business record requiring a custodian if offered by Plaintiffs; Doc. 34 is judicially noticeable as a court record but its background footnote is not a finding
notes: The distinction in the gap column is the organizing point of the funding analysis.

proposition: HELOC loan proceeds were actually delivered to Plaintiffs or their creditors, on identified dates and in identified amounts
what_the_document_actually_shows: NOTHING IN THIS MANIFEST SPEAKS TO THIS. No closing statement, settlement statement, wire confirmation, disbursement schedule, or creditor payoff confirmation is among the sources.
what_is_claimed_from_it: That the loan was funded (Defendants' implicit position) or that it was not (a theory implicit in Plaintiffs' fraud allegations)
gap_between_the_two: Total. The court identified this as the question on which many claims depend, and the record before this system contains no evidence either way.
notes: Confidence high that the record is silent, which is itself the finding. See GAP-001. Any assertion in either direction on the present record would be invented.

proposition: MERS transferred its interest in the Security Deed to MEB Loan Trust VIII in 2024
what_the_document_actually_shows: The court's background footnote states that 'In 2024, MERS transferred interest in the Security Deed to MEB Loan Trust VIII'
what_is_claimed_from_it: That MEB holds the security deed and has authority to foreclose (Defendants) or that the assignment is void and MEB lacks standing (Plaintiffs)
gap_between_the_two: Large. The footnote records that a transfer occurred; it says nothing about the assignment's validity, the chain of note indorsements, or authority to exercise the power of sale. The recorded assignment itself is not in this manifest, so neither its recitals nor its execution can be examined.
admissibility_concerns: The recorded instrument would be self-authenticating; the footnote is not the instrument
notes: A background footnote in an order deciding a remand motion is weak support for a contested ownership question. Obtain the recorded assignment.

proposition: Plaintiffs remitted a $5,200.00 wire payment that Defendants received and failed to credit
what_the_document_actually_shows: No source in this manifest shows a $5,200.00 payment. The servicer's 5-page ledger, which records suspense and unapplied credits as small as $71.78 and as large as $19,588.88, contains no $5,200.00 entry in any column or period.
what_is_claimed_from_it: That Plaintiffs performed under the contract and that Defendants misapplied or diverted a payment - the factual core of the breach, RESPA payment-application, and FDCPA theories
gap_between_the_two: Total, and adverse. This is not merely an unsupported allegation; the document a factfinder would consult first affirmatively does not contain it.
notes: See CON-001 and GAP-002. This is the highest-priority factual gap in the matter.

proposition: Plaintiffs submitted qualifying Notices of Error and Requests for Information to Shellpoint at its designated address
what_the_document_actually_shows: The 03/02/2026 letter identifies the designated error-resolution address as 'SLS Default - SMS P.O. Box 10826 Greenville, SC 29603-0826' and responds to a CFPB-portal complaint
what_is_claimed_from_it: That RESPA's notice-of-error machinery was triggered and Shellpoint failed to comply
gap_between_the_two: Large. The letter establishes what the designated address IS. It does not establish that any NOE or RFI was sent there. No NOE or RFI document is in this manifest, and the only documented channel is the CFPB portal - which is not the designated address.
notes: Whether CFPB-portal routing satisfies 12 C.F.R. 1024.35(c) is a legal question, not a factual one, and should be researched before the claim is repleaded. See GAP-003.

proposition: Defendants furnished inaccurate data to the consumer reporting agencies and failed to investigate reasonably after CRA notice
what_the_document_actually_shows: No credit report, tradeline printout, ACDV form, e-OSCAR record, or dispute response is in this manifest. The specific figures pleaded (a $0.00 balance with $25,495.00 past due in November 2024; a $173,839.00 balance on a $149,650.00 limit in October 2025) appear only in the pleading.
what_is_claimed_from_it: That the furnished data was facially impossible and that the 1681s-2(b) duty was triggered and breached
gap_between_the_two: Total as to the data, and as to the CRA-notice element, which 1681s-2(b) requires. One partially corroborating thread exists: the ledger shows principal fixed at $140,288.02 from 12/21/23 onward, so a reported balance of $173,839.00 would not match the servicer's own principal - but total debt including interest and fees might, and the ledger does not compute accrued interest.
notes: See GAP-004. Note SRC-012 records a Shellpoint statement that it 'places a hold on credit reporting on any mortgage account for which a dispute is received' - a party statement that may be useful on the furnishing timeline.

proposition: NewRez LLC d/b/a Shellpoint is a debt collector within the meaning of 15 U.S.C. 1692a(6)
what_the_document_actually_shows: Shellpoint's own letter states: 'Newrez LLC dba Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing is a debt collector. This is an attempt to collect a debt and any information obtained will be used for that purpose.'
what_is_claimed_from_it: That Shellpoint is subject to the FDCPA
gap_between_the_two: Small. A party's own FDCPA disclosure is strong evidence of its self-characterization and is a party admission. It is not conclusive of the legal status, which turns on the statutory definition and on whether the debt was in default when acquired - but it is very good support.
admissibility_concerns: Party admission under Fed. R. Evid. 801(d)(2); authentication straightforward as a document produced by the party
notes: One of the few propositions in this matter that is genuinely well supported on the present record.

proposition: Foreclosure-related fees and costs were charged to the account from May 2024 through February 2026 while no payment was applied
what_the_document_actually_shows: The ledger records a continuous series of Property Inspection, Title, Attorney, FC Costs, Certified Mail, and BPO/Appraisal disbursements from 05/06/24 through 02/27/26, with principal frozen at $140,288.02 throughout, an ending Late Charge Balance of $624.00, and an ending Unapplied Balance of $1,899.56
what_is_claimed_from_it: That Defendants extracted fees while refusing to apply tendered funds
gap_between_the_two: Moderate. The charges and the frozen principal are exactly what the document shows. That the fees were UNAUTHORIZED, or that funds were wrongly withheld from application, is not shown - the ledger also shows three of the four 2025 web payments were reversed with NSF events, which would ordinarily justify non-application.
admissibility_concerns: Business record; custodian needed if Plaintiffs offer it
notes: The one payment that was NOT reversed - $1,899.56 on 05/17/25 - sat in suspense and still appears as the ending Unapplied Balance ten months later. That single retained-but-unapplied payment is a cleaner RESPA payment-application fact than the $5,200.00 wire, and it is documented.

proposition: A binding loan modification agreement was executed and Defendants repudiated it
what_the_document_actually_shows: No loan modification agreement, approval letter, trial-plan document, or loss-mitigation denial is in this manifest. Doc. 34 at 3 n.4 states the opposite direction: 'Loss mitigation efforts explored between Shellpoint and Plaintiffs dating back to August 2024 have been unsuccessful.'
what_is_claimed_from_it: That Plaintiffs were contractually protected and that foreclosure breached an executed agreement
gap_between_the_two: Total, and the only judicial statement in the record points the other way.
notes: See GAP-005. A dual-tracking theory under 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 also requires a COMPLETE loss-mitigation application, which is likewise undocumented here.

proposition: Defendants published false foreclosure advertisements causing special damages
what_the_document_actually_shows: No published notice of sale, no legal-organ advertisement, and no document evidencing the Mercer Advisors offer or its rescission is in this manifest.
what_is_claimed_from_it: That the attempted-wrongful-foreclosure elements are met
gap_between_the_two: Total on both the publication and the special-damages elements. Georgia's attempted wrongful foreclosure tort requires a published false advertisement AND special damages; neither is documented.
notes: See GAP-007 and GAP-008. The employment offer and its rescission are documentable facts that the client should be able to supply directly.

proposition: The recorded Assignment of Security Deed contains false statements about ownership
what_the_document_actually_shows: The assignment itself is not in this manifest. Its book and page are pleaded but the instrument has not been examined.
what_is_claimed_from_it: That the assignment is void and slanders title
gap_between_the_two: Total. Falsity cannot be assessed without the instrument, and Doc. 34 at 3 n.4 records the transfer as having occurred.
admissibility_concerns: The recorded instrument would be self-authenticating once obtained
notes: Obtaining the recorded assignment from the Forsyth County Clerk is a public-record step requiring no discovery. See GAP-009.

proposition: An actual justiciable controversy exists as to the amount owed and the authority to foreclose
supporting_pinpoints: Doc. 34 at 4, 26; letter p.1; ledger totals p.5
what_the_document_actually_shows: The parties actively dispute the balance and the right to foreclose; Doc. 34 at 4 records Defendants' plan to re-notice a sale; Doc. 34 at 26 imposes a 60-day notice obligation on that plan
gap_between_the_two: Small as to the existence of a controversy. Large as to injunctive relief: Doc. 34 at 25 held there is no imminent irreparable harm with no sale scheduled, and that reasoning will recur.
notes: The 60-day notice obligation is the practical substitute for the injunction that was denied, and it is the most valuable thing Plaintiffs currently hold.

proposition: Three of four web payments tendered in May-June 2025 were reversed with NSF events, and one was retained in suspense and never applied
supporting_pinpoints: p.2, rows dated 05/02/25 through 06/25/25; totals block p.5
what_the_document_actually_shows: Four Web Payments of $1,899.56 each on 05/02, 05/10, 05/17 and 06/18/2025. Those of 05/02, 05/10 and 06/18 were reversed under Rev Code 2, each paired with an NSF Fee Assessment showing a $0.00 amount. The 05/17/25 payment was not reversed, and the totals block shows 'Ending Unapplied Balance $1,899.56' as of the 03/10/26 print.
what_is_claimed_from_it: Plaintiffs: that payments were tendered and refused. Defendants: that the payments failed.
gap_between_the_two: Real but narrow, and it cuts both ways. Three reversals with NSF events support Defendants. The fourth payment does not: it was received, never reversed, and sat unapplied in suspense for roughly ten months while foreclosure fees accrued.
notes: This is the strongest documented payment-application fact in the matter, and it comes from the defendants' own record rather than from the pleading. It should be developed in place of, or alongside, the $5,200.00 theory.
